title: Westpac reveals AI cut data warehouse migration cost from $70m to $35m
headline: Westpac uses AI to halve St.George data warehouse migration costs to $35m
summary: Westpac leveraged AI to accelerate the migration of its legacy St.George data warehouse. This initiative reduced the project cost from a budgeted $70 million to approximately $35 million and completed the migration more than two years ahead of schedule. The project also developed a reusable AI data migration capability for future applications across the bank.
why_it_matters: This case study demonstrates a concrete, quantifiable benefit of AI in a critical operational context for a major Australian financial institution, highlighting the need for robust governance and assurance frameworks for such deployments.

quotes.text: Westpac says AI-accelerated migration of the legacy St.George data warehouse cut costs from a budgeted $70 million to around $35 million.
The team used AI tools to speed up code conversion, testing and documentation.
The project produced a reusable AI data migration capability that Westpac expects to apply to other migrations for further benefits.

dates_mentioned.what: Full year ended for statutory net profit report
dates_mentioned.quote: Westpac reported a statutory net profit of $6.8 billion for the full year ended September 30 2026

classification.significance_reason: A major Australian bank demonstrated significant, quantifiable cost savings and efficiency gains from an AI deployment in a core operational area, creating a reusable capability.
